rows: Half dollar-size hail was reported in the southern part of the county.
Penny to quarter-size hail reported at CR 403 and 410.

Trees were blown down in roads in and around Palestine. In Neches, a 68-foot porch was entirely ripped off of a house and was strewn 100 feet away. Shingles were also torn off the roof. Also in Neches, more than 15 large trees and numerous power lines were uprooted near FM 2574, …
Numerous trees were split and blown down along U.S. 79 and CR 367 between Palestine and Neches. Tree limbs and lawn furniture were blown across yards, and a window of a house was broken.
Spotters confirmed a tornado on the ground west of Tennessee Colony and south of Bethel. Some structural damage was reported.

Structural damage to homes was reported near the intersection of FM 1990 and Highway 294. Roofs were partially removed, trees were blown onto houses, and trees and power lines blown down. One house on CR 2137 just off FM 1990 had the ceiling cave in. In addition, the front porch …
Downed trees and power lines blocked numerous areas of downtown Palestine including South Magnolia at Bowers Street and Stephanie Drive, and Pecan, West Carolina, Timberline, and East Neches Streets.

A tornado formed near the intersection of CR 403 and CR 404 and moved north to near Elmwood, causing damage to homes, trees, sheds, and power lines. Trees were split, twisted, and uprooted. The county judge surveyed the damage and found the worst to be between FM 315 and CR 404.
A roof was blown off of a carport near Tennessee Colony. Numerous trees and power poles were blown down.
Several large trees were blown down on roads in Tucker and Neches.
Quarter-size hail was two-inches deep along Highway 294 between Tucker and Elkhart.
Hail the size of half-dollars was reported at Crystal Lake.
More than fifty trees were broken or uprooted in the Concord community.
Quarter-size hail was reported in Elmtown.
Large tree limbs were blown down.
Trees were blown down in and just south of town. Large limbs fell on roads and power lines.
A power pole was blown onto a car.

A tower was damaged at a prison and an eighteen wheeler tractor-trailer was blown over. On FM 321, four houses had shingles missing, two sheds were damaged, and numerous trees had been blown down and some had their tops sheared off. Power lines were downed by trees and large limb…
Hail as large as hen eggs was reported. The hail broke siding off a home and damaged trim around windows.
A 70 MPH wind gust was measured in Tennessee Colony.

A tornado touched down just west of Tennessee Colony and moved towards Montalba. A metal roof was removed from a mobile home on FM 2709 and a barn was heavily damaged. Numerous trees were twisted and broken with their leaves stripped off. On Highway 287, a mobile home was damaged…
Half dollar-size hail was reported near Montalba.
The roof was blown off the drive-thru section of a bank. Trees and power lines were also blown down.

Numerous trees were knocked down in the Elkhart, Slocum, and Denson Springs areas. An elderly resident had to be helped out of her mobile home on CR 1231 in the Elkhart area after a tree fell on it. Some of the trees that were uprooted were several feet in diameter.

A home on HWY 287 south of Elkhart and about 10 miles north of Grapeland had its front porch ripped off and half of its roof torn off. The roof was laying about a 100 yards from the house. Water damage occurred inside the house as a result.
